promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 6 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: The 20-miler shows your fitness is there, but 53 miles against a planned 38 is too big a jump to repeat. This week steps back to about 40 miles, with the same sessions and a firm stop distance on every run.

flags.title: Plan overrun
flags.detail: You ran 53 mi against 38 planned. That included a run on Monday's rest day, a fourth threshold rep and a 20 mi long run instead of 15. Treat every distance on the plan as a cap this week.

flags.title: Load jump
flags.detail: Distance rose from 37 to 53 mi in one week, and your effort score was almost double your recent average. Feeling fine now does not clear it, because calves and tendons adapt slower than fitness.

flags.title: Calf tightness
flags.detail: Your calves were tight on Sunday night. Check them Monday and Tuesday, and if they stay tight or get worse, swap Wednesday's session for an easy run.

flags.title: Long run effort
flags.detail: Your 20 miler spent 88% of its time in zone 3, about 10 beats above your easy days. Keep Sunday's long run under 145 bpm so it stays easy.

flags.title: Group run distance
flags.detail: You kept going to 20 with your club mates. Agree the distance before you start on Sunday and stop there.

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer:
Not at this volume, so the plan takes you back to about 40 miles this week. You felt fine because your heart and lungs adapt in days, while calves, tendons and joints take weeks. The tight calves on Sunday night are the first sign of that gap.

Keep the way you ran: easy days at heart rate 139, steady threshold reps and an even long run. Add distance in steps of about 10 percent, with a lighter week every third or fourth week. That puts your next 18 to 20 miler around Sun Oct 11, and the feeling that you have turned a corner will still be there on race day.

new.analysis:
You ran longer than planned on six of seven days, and this week is built to absorb that extra 15 miles.

| Day | Planned | Ran |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mon Sep 7 | rest | 4 mi easy |
| Tue Sep 8 | 6 mi easy | 7 mi |
| Wed Sep 9 | 8 mi, 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00/mi | 9 mi, 4 reps at 7:55/mi |
| Thu Sep 10 | 5 mi easy | 7 mi |
| Fri Sep 11 | rest | rest |
| Sat Sep 12 | 4 mi easy | 6 mi |
| Sun Sep 13 | 15 mi easy, heart rate under 150 | 20 mi, average heart rate 149 |
| Total | 38 mi | 53 mi |

The running itself was good, which is why the overrun is tempting. Every easy run sat at heart rate 139 and about 9:50/mi, the four threshold reps showed no fade, and the 20 miler held 9:52/mi in the first half and 9:54/mi in the second. Pain stayed at 0/10 all week.

The risk is the size of the jump, not the quality of the running. Weekly distance went from 37 mi to 53 mi, about 1.5 times your four-week average of 35 mi. Before that, the knee, the heat and the broken AC held you to 24 and 27 mi, so the base under this jump is thin.

The 20 miler is banked, and it is the biggest piece of marathon-specific work you will do. You do not need another one for a few weeks, and a lighter long run now lets your legs turn it into fitness. The 54% easy share against the 80% target comes from that long run, not from your easy days, which sat in zone 2.

Forty miles is still a step up from the 37 before the spike, so the build does not stall. From the week of Sep 21 – 27 I will add a medium-long run during the week and bring marathon-pace segments back into the long run. Pace for under 3:45 is about 8:35/mi, and your 8:34/mi reps on Wed Sep 2 were right on it. A last long run of 18 to 20 mi around Sun Oct 11 comes before the taper.

The plan this week caps every run. The reason is simple: the days you feel best are the days you are most likely to add miles, and that is when a build gets derailed.

Stop at three reps and run no faster than 8:00/mi, or swap it for 6 mi easy if your calves are still tight on Tuesday night. Threshold work is this phase's key session, and three reps gives the benefit without last week's extra load.

settingsProposalBullets: Change "no injuries in the last two years" to note outside-of-right-knee pain in mid-August that settled within about a week, so I keep watching it as mileage rises.
Add that you tend to add distance when you feel good or run with club mates, so plan lines will carry a firm stop distance.
Add that your easy-run heart rate is about 139 and your long-run heart rate runs about 10 beats higher at the same pace.
Add that marathon pace for under 3:45 is about 8:35/mi and your threshold pace is about 8:00/mi.

safetyCallouts.title: Calf tightness after the 20 miler.
safetyCallouts.body: Tight calves after a big jump are common, but check them Monday and Tuesday. If they stay tight, get worse or turn into pain, skip the session and see a physio. The same applies if the outside of your right knee starts to hurt again.
